diagnostics.title: LIST MAY BE SHARED
diagnostics.message:
`update` changes `model.todos` in place, and the checker cannot show that
nothing else still holds the list.

363|    Tea.element
        ^^^^^^^^^^^ the runtime hands `update` the model here

Compute what a command or a subscription needs from the list before it is made,
so that it keeps that value and not the list; or hand it a copy, made with
`List.copy`.

This is a limit of the checker, not proof of sharing: at some message the
runtime keeps it: a command or a subscription holds it, or update escapes it.

diagnostics.title: LIST CHANGED WHILE STILL IN USE
diagnostics.message:
`current.trail ++ other.trail` adds to the end of `current.trail` itself, but
`current.trail` is read again afterwards.

91|        ( weapon, explosion ) = Weapon.shoot current (current.trail ++ other.trail)
                                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the list is changed in place here
92|        ( { current | weapon = weapon }, explosion )
               ^^^^^^^ and `current.trail` is read here, after the change

If the list were changed in place, `current.trail` would see the change when it
is read on line 92.

To change a copy and leave `current.trail` as it was, copy it there:

91|        ( weapon, explosion ) = Weapon.shoot current (List.copy current.trail ++ other.trail)

This is sharing the checker can see: `current.trail` is read on line 92, after
the change.

diagnostics.title: LIST CHANGED WHILE STILL IN USE
diagnostics.message:
`Bike.shoot` changes a list it is handed in place, but `red.trail` still holds
the old list and is read afterwards.

135|            { red, green } = model.bikes
                  ^^^ `red.trail` keeps the list here
136|            ( redUpdated, redShot ) = Bike.shoot key { current = red, other = green }
                                          ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ the list is changed in place here
137|            ( greenUpdated, greenShot ) = Bike.shoot key { current = green, other = red }
                                                                                        ^^^ and `red.trail` is read here, after the change

If the list were changed in place, `red.trail` would see the change when it is
read on line 137.

Or, if `red.trail` only needs the list as it was, read it before line 136.

Copy the list with `List.copy` before it is changed, so the change cannot reach
anything else that holds it.

This is sharing the checker can see: `red.trail` is read on line 137, after the
change.

diagnostics.title: PREPEND IN LOOP
diagnostics.message:
This puts elements in front of `acc`, the accumulator this `List.foldr` hands
back to its callback, so it happens at every step:

    [ (…), …acc ]

A list is an array, so every step copies the whole accumulator, and the loop
takes time that grows with the square of the list's length. Add at the end
instead, which takes the same short time at every step:

    [ …acc, (…) ]

`List.foldr` hands over the last element first, so to keep the order write
the loop as `List.foldl`, which hands over the first element first.

If the prepend is meant — the list stays short — give the new list a name
first, and this warning goes.

diagnostics.title: PREPEND IN LOOP
diagnostics.message:
This puts elements in front of `acc`, which this function hands back to
itself, so it happens at every step of a loop:

    [ (…), …acc ]

A list is an array, so every step copies the whole accumulator, and the loop
takes time that grows with the square of the list's length. Add at the end
instead, which takes the same short time at every step:

    [ …acc, (…) ]

That keeps the elements in the order they arrive, so the `List.reverse` that
put a prepended result back in order is no longer needed.

If the prepend is meant — the list stays short — give the new list a name
first, and this warning goes.

diagnostics.title: TOP-LEVEL LIST CHANGED
diagnostics.message:
`update` changes `model.bikes.green.trail` and `model.bikes.red.trail` in place,
but when the program starts each is `Game.initBikes`, a top-level value.

12|    Tea.document
       ^^^^^^^^^^^^ the runtime hands `update` the model here

`Game.initBikes` is defined in examples/bike-wars/src/Game.beni:

54|initBikes =
   ^^^^^^^^^ the top-level list is defined here

A top-level value is shared by every part of the program and never changes:
changed in place, it would change for every part that reads it.

Build `Game.initBikes` where the program starts, so that its lists are new ones,
or copy each list it holds there with `List.copy`.

This is the language's rule for top-level values, whether or not anything else
reads the list.
